set.approach: Park at the pullout on Highway 16 that also serves Morro Bluffs and Morro Slabs, a little past the Overlander trail parking and before the road crosses the Athabasca. Walk the Overlander trail, then take the fainter trail that branches left toward the wall; cairns mark the way, and the approach spurs fork left again toward individual routes. Continue past the broad chimney of Guide's Route. Spring Break starts to the left of that chimney, after a short scramble up to a ledge where the first bolt is.
set.descent_text: Walk off. From the last anchors, scramble up broken ground until you reach a forest, then trend toward the rock wall and left to pick up the descent trail. The trail back down is long and slippery.

review.notes: Route page gives start and top-out scramble; area page gives parking, trail and walk-off descent. Distances and times left out (single source).

set.approach: Use the small parking area on the east side of the second Athabasca River bridge. A steep path from the lot climbs to the top of the slabs, and the routes are reached by walking along the top of the rock; Aqua Size is the southernmost line on the River Rock section and is the one line there you can walk to without rappelling in.

review.notes: Area page for parking and path; route page for position. No descent stated.

Deep Blue starts below the southern metal post left from bridge construction; rappel from the top onto a grassy ledge, which has a two-bolt anchor and is where the climbing starts.

review.notes: Area page for parking and path; route page for start.

set.approach: Park at the large cairn on top of the embankment beside the Spray Lakes road, at the buttress closest to the road. Scramble up the embankment, where a faint climber's trail leads into the trees and joins the High Rockies gravel trail. Turn right along the gravel trail to a talus field with a few cairns, then turn uphill on a faint path with long traversing switchbacks, which becomes more obvious halfway to the wall. Look for the big right-facing corner at the contact between the grey and yellow rock. A flat ledge with two bolts there is a place to gear up, and the route starts a short way below it, usually marked by a small cairn.
set.descent_text: The route is equipped for rappelling, with chained anchors and a single ring at each station. Loose gravel and rock sit on the ledges, so keep the ropes clear of them and watch for rockfall onto the party below. A walk-off by the scramble route to climber's right is the other way down.

review.notes: Route page: approach, anchors, rappel and scramble walk-off; area page confirms the buttress closest to the road.

set.approach: Park at the pullout on the west side of Highway 93 in front of Hector Creek. Cross the road and look for the Mount Hector trail, which starts on the south bank of the drainage. It rises through forest along the left edge of an avalanche bowl and ends above a waterfall. Cross the creek there and enter the small hanging valley between Mount Andromache and Little Hector. Follow cairns to a two-tiered tree island, then cairns and goat trails up and left across a series of benches and an easy gully to the upper benches. Cross left (northwest) over a bowl with a large boulder, follow the steps of a dry watercourse up the basin to the base of the towers, and go to the farthest-left bowl rather than around toward the highway. The right-hand tower is easily mistaken for Achilles Spire; the spire has a small crumbly tower on its left, a sharp pointed tower on its right, and narrowing drainages on both sides, with a large black roof beside the right-hand drainage. The route starts below and left of that roof, at a one-bolt station on a small ledge among smaller overlapping overhangs.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route. The line is set up for rappels from bolted stations, with a few short scrambles on ledges between stations and a walk around the buttress partway down. Some of the rappels run over steep or overhanging rock and the rope pulls with friction, so knot the ends. From the bottom, follow the cairns back down to the trail.

review.notes: Route page for the whole approach and rappel descent; area page for the parking location. Rappel and station counts left out (single source).

set.approach: Follow the Spencer Creek trail through forest. After it opens out, climb beside the right bank of a drainage, ford it, and move up and left below low cliff bands to an easy break. Continue up and right, then left through a gap in the trees, and at the top of the vegetation pick up a game trail rising diagonally left onto the connecting ridge that joins Little Lougheed to Lougheed II. Follow the ridge, traverse right under the cliff bands to a scree bowl, and climb its left margin; the drainage that descends from the bowl is the alternative, and both are tedious. The route begins at the far left end of the big cliff bands, with the first bolt visible up and left.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the west ridge. Follow the ridge to the summit of Lougheed II and descend by the scramble route. Rappelling the line is possible with double ropes, but the anchors have no rings.

review.notes: One route page carries the approach and descent; area page confirms a scramble route exists.

set.approach: From the Fireside parking area, reached by the Highway 1A exit west of Banff, follow the trail across the creek to a junction and take the Edith Pass trail. At the next signed junction, follow the Cory Pass trail, which climbs gently through forest beneath the south and centre summits of Mount Edith. Once the trees thin, a brief drop brings you to scree beneath the north summit of Mount Edith and Mount Louis, where the east face routes begin.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit. Descend by rappelling the peak's north side from bolted anchors, beginning from the anchor above a gentle gully just below the summit. Partway down, a short easy ramp on climber's left of the gully leads to the next anchor; an earlier ramp looks similar but is the wrong one. Below the last rappels a steep trail leads to the base of the mountain.

review.notes: Route page: east face of the Diamond, onto the summit. Area page: approach and the north side rappel descent. Rappel count and rope lengths left out.

set.approach: Park at the Sunshine Village lot. Cross the staff parking area heading west to its far end; a trail leaves from the back right corner by the sheds. Follow it through trees alongside the creek for a couple of minutes, then it turns right and ascends over slabby rock to the cliff foot, on the right side of the waterfall called Bourgeau Left. Flirting with the Bosch begins immediately to the left of a leaning, left-facing corner.

review.notes: Route page for approach and start. No descent stated on this route.

set.approach: Park at the Sunshine Village lot. Cross the staff parking area heading west to its far end; a trail leaves from the back right corner by the sheds. review.notes: Own page says rappel down the line; start position from own page. Approach from the neighbouring slab-route page for the same slab, which is an approach shared by the wall.

set.approach: Leave the car where the power line clearing begins and hike uphill to the south-east facing buttresses. The route starts as a bolted sport pitch that ends at a pair of ring bolts, and the climbing continues all the way to the summit.
set.descent_text: The upper cliff has rappel stations on a line separate from the climbing route. The first pitch can be split at a rappel station to the left of its halfway point, and bolts on the small headwall above the second pitch are used for rappelling. Above the upper cliff it is a scramble along or below the ridge to the summit.

review.notes: One route page plus area page. Times, gain and rope lengths left out.

set.approach: From the Maligne Lake Road, a little past the picnic area, look for two boulders on the left. The trail climbs beside a boulder field to the slab. The route starts from trees with flagging tape, some distance south of the corner at the north end of the slab.
set.descent_text: Walk off, or rappel the route on its bolted anchors.

review.notes: Route page for start and both descent options; area page for the trail. Distances left out.

set.approach: Park at the pullout at Leech Lake on Highway 93A, south of Jasper past Athabasca Falls, or at the next small pullout beyond it, and follow the maintained trail into the forest to the Lost Boys cliffline. Walk along the cliffline to the very obvious cave formed by a boulder pile, which you can pass under or around, and scramble onto its roof. The route is the left-hand bolt line, starting from the roof of the cave.
set.descent_text: The anchor is a pair of rap hangers set back a little from the edge; rappel to clean it.

review.notes: Route and Rave Cave page for start and anchor; Lost Boys page for parking and trail.

set.approach: Park on the shoulder where the ridge meets Highway 16 at the Rec Beach pullout, or at the larger pullout a little earlier along the road, which also serves the trailhead for Roche Miette and Shredder Reef. From the Rec Beach pullout a trail leaves through a break in the trees below the steep grassy hill and runs along the base of the boulder field, turns left into the willows, and winds toward the wall with a few sharp turns and a single switchback, then runs along the full length of the wall. Skip the first fork, which is the Road Rage turnoff, and keep following the main trail for a few minutes until it reaches the wall, then climb the short steep hill. The route starts a little further along, next to a small alcove where the cliff meets the ground.
set.descent_text: Two ways down. Walk off: scramble fourth class down the ridge, or work away from the ridge toward the Rec Beach trail, heading for the top of the second rocky hill, where the trees get thicker. Drop down behind that outcrop and turn right into the gully with a lone tall tree at its mouth, and stay on the trail down the whole gully instead of following goat trails and flagging to the left. Or rappel the route, which is fully equipped; one upper pitch cannot be rappelled, so there are two separate rappel lines depending on whether you are above or below it. A long rope is needed. Tie knots in the rope ends.

review.notes: Route page for approach, start, walk-off and rappel lines; area page for parking.

set.approach: Park on the shoulder where the ridge meets Highway 16 at the Rec Beach pullout, or at the larger pullout a little earlier along the road, which also serves the trailhead for Roche Miette and Shredder Reef. From the Rec Beach pullout a trail leaves through a break in the trees below the steep grassy hill and runs along the base of the boulder field, turns left into the willows, and winds toward the wall with a few sharp turns and a single switchback, then runs along the full length of the wall. Shortly beyond the switchback, a small cairn marks the turnoff for Road Rage; follow it uphill until the white slab is visible on your right.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route with a long rope and tie knots in the ends; on the last pitch begin on the bolt-line side of the arete, then swing across below the crux to reach the anchor. A fourth-class walk-off also exists: from the final anchor take the exposed grassy ledge to the broader ridge, scramble down the right side of the ridge through cliff bands, then work left to the grassy gully.

review.notes: Route page for approach, start, rappel and walk-off; area page for parking.
